# lookout audit upgrades

Upgrade and patch readiness, read from the cloud provider and cluster upgrade-blocker catalogue: how far the control plane and its node pools are behind what the provider publishes (or --target-version), whether anything is set up to close that gap on its own — release channel, node auto-upgrade and auto-repair, a maintenance window, active maintenance exclusions, node images on the removed Docker runtime, and upgrade notifications — plus in-cluster upgrade blockers (deprecated/removed APIs in use, fail-closed admission webhooks on upgrade-critical paths, and PodDisruptionBudgets that allow zero disruptions during node drain). Without a provider capability or --target-version it reports an explicit unavailable rather than silence.

MCP tool: `k8s_audit_upgrades` (MCP profile: `audit`)

## Usage

    lookout audit upgrades [flags]

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--target-version` | — | target Kubernetes version (e.g. 1.32 or 1.32.1-gke.1000) to evaluate upgrade readiness and API removals against, overriding the provider's published target |
| `--policy` | — | path to a YAML posture policy file |
| `--profile` | — | built-in posture profile: default\|strict\|onboarding\|gke-autopilot |
| `--only` | — | comma-separated check kind or kind/reason globs to run exclusively |
| `--skip` | — | comma-separated check kind or kind/reason globs to skip |
| `--min-severity` | — | minimum finding severity to emit: info\|warning\|critical |
| `--set` | — | comma-separated check parameter overrides (<kind>.<param>=<val>) |

## Common flags (every lookout command)

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--namespace` | — | limit the scan to one namespace |
| `-A` | — | scan all namespaces |
| `--workload` | — | target one workload as <Kind>/<namespace>/<name>, e.g. Deployment/prod/api |
| `--since` | — | how far back to look (0 = command default) |
| `--format` | logfmt | output format: logfmt\|json (one record per line either way) |
| `--timeout` | 10s | abort the invocation after this long (exit 1) |
| `--kubeconfig` | — | path to a kubeconfig file, instead of $KUBECONFIG / ~/.kube/config |
| `--kubeconfig-dir` | — | directory of kubeconfig files to fan out across (mutually exclusive with --kubeconfig); each finding is stamped with cluster=<label> and the summary reports clusters=<n> |
| `--context` | — | kubeconfig context to read, instead of its current-context. Selects a cluster for THIS invocation only — nothing is written back — so concurrent invocations can target different clusters. Reported as context=<name> in the summary line |
| `--contexts` | — | comma-separated kubeconfig contexts to fan out across, or '*' for every context in the selected kubeconfig(s) (mutually exclusive with --context); each finding is stamped with cluster=<label> and the summary reports clusters=<n> |
| `--concurrency` | 4 | maximum concurrent cluster executions when fanning out with --contexts or --kubeconfig-dir |
| `--exemptions` | — | path to a git-reviewed exemption file (YAML); covered findings are ANNOTATED with their reason and expiry and counted as exempt=<n> in the summary, never dropped |

## Finding kinds

Every `kind=` this command can emit, and the severities it carries them at. Nothing else appears in its output; a kind absent from a run means the check looked and found nothing.

| Kind | Severity | Claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.version_behind` | critical, warning, info | the control plane or a node pool is behind what the provider publishes, or a node pool has skewed from the control plane; info while the gap is still within the supported skew |
| `audit.upgrade_unmanaged` | warning | nothing will close that gap on its own: no release channel, or node auto-upgrade/auto-repair off |
| `audit.upgrade_blocked` | critical, warning, info | an active maintenance exclusion, a node image on the removed Docker runtime, a removed API in use, a fail-closed upgrade-path webhook, or a zero-disruption PDB will stop or stall the upgrade when it comes |
| `audit.deprecated_api_in_use` | critical, warning | a cluster resource was last applied with a Kubernetes API version that is deprecated or removed in the target minor release |
| `audit.upgrade_unattended` | info | upgrades will happen with nobody watching: no maintenance window, or no upgrade notifications |
| `cloud.unavailable` | info | the cloud capability this check needs is unavailable, so nothing was examined — an explicit degradation record, never silence (§2, §11) |

## Output fields

Beyond the shared envelope fields (`kind`, `severity`, `namespace`, `kind_of_object`, `name`, `reason`, `message`, `fingerprint`, `exempt_reason`, `exempt_expires`):

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `cluster` | on a node-pool finding: the cluster the pool belongs to, so the record stands alone |
| `version` | the current version of the finding's subject — the control plane's, or the node pool's |
| `target_version` | the version the provider would move this cluster to: its channel's upgrade target where one is published, otherwise the channel's default (or --target-version) |
| `control_plane_version` | on a node-pool skew finding: the control-plane version the pool is measured against |
| `minor_versions_behind` | how many minor releases separate the two versions |
| `channel` | the release channel the cluster is subscribed to, and the one whose published versions the comparison used; `none` when it is subscribed to no channel |
| `image_type` | the provider's name for the node image the pool runs |
| `exclusion` | the operator's name for the maintenance exclusion currently in force |
| `scope` | how much of the upgrade stream that exclusion holds back: all-upgrades, minor-upgrades or minor-and-node-upgrades |
| `ends` | when the exclusion lifts, or `end-of-support` for one that runs until the cluster's version leaves support |
| `days_remaining` | how much longer the exclusion has left to run |
| `api_version` | on a deprecated-API finding: the deprecated or removed group/version in use |
| `removed_in` | on a deprecated-API finding: the Kubernetes major.minor release that removes the API |
| `replacement` | on a deprecated-API finding: the successor group/version to migrate to |
| `webhook` | on a webhook upgrade-blocker finding: the individual webhook entry within the configuration |
| `webhook_group` | on a webhook upgrade-blocker finding: the upgrade-critical operation group intercepted (drain-eviction, pod-creation, node-lease, kubelet-csr, csi-storage, control-plane-rbac) |
| `service` | on a webhook upgrade-blocker finding: the namespace/name of the backing Service |
| `timeout_seconds` | on a webhook timeout finding: the configured webhook timeout in seconds, or default(10) when unset |
| `replicas` | on a single-replica webhook or PDB finding: the replica count of the backing or protected workload |
| `min_available` | on a PDB upgrade-blocker finding: the configured minAvailable threshold |
| `max_unavailable` | on a PDB upgrade-blocker finding: the configured maxUnavailable threshold |
| `disruptions_allowed` | on a PDB upgrade-blocker finding: the live disruptionsAllowed count |
| `node_pools` | summary note: node pools examined — the cluster itself is the other unit `scanned` counts |
| `capability` | cloud.unavailable: the provider capability this command needed (cluster-config) |
| `provider` | cloud.unavailable: the provider that was asked |
| `unavailable` | summary-line note (§2 marker): why the cloud read could not be served |

## Output contract

Output: one finding per line (logfmt; --format=json for one JSON object
per line), keys in fixed order; healthy resources emit nothing. The final
line is always the summary: scanned=<n> findings=<n> elapsed=<d> —
findings=0 with a summary present means "scanned and healthy"; a stream
without a summary line is void. Exit 0 data, 1 runtime error (diagnostics
on stderr only), 2 usage.

## Examples

```lookout
lookout audit upgrades
lookout audit upgrades --target-version=1.32
lookout audit upgrades --format=json
lookout audit upgrades --exemptions=exemptions.yaml
```
